utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Case IT-04-74-PT, the Prosecutor against Jadranko Prlic, Bruno Stojic, Slobodan Praljak, Milivoj Petkovic, Valentin Coric, and Berislav Pusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. May I first have the appearances. The Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Kenneth Scott for the Office of the Prosecutor. With me today are Ms. Josee D'Aoust. Our case manager, Denise Gustin, Roeland Bos, Garlone Egels, Vasily Poryvaev, and Miguel Longone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Scott. Then as far as the accused are concerned, Defence, could I invite you not only to tell your name, but also whether you are defending with co-counsel and who you are defending. I just start at the first row at the left, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SALAHOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Camil Salahovic, attorney-at-law from Zagreb, Republic of Croatia, appearing for the accused Mr. Jadranko Prlic. I have with me Mr. Zelimir Par, as co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salahovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLUJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Zeljko Olujic, lead counsel for the accused Bruno Stojic. I will be appearing alone today because we still don't have a co-counsel on our team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Next row.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Bozidar Kovacic. I am a lead counsel of the Defence of Mr. Slobodan Praljak. I'm an attorney from Croatia, from Rijeka, and with me is co-counsel Ms. Nika Pinter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Vesna Alaburic, attorney-at-law from Zagreb, representing Mr. Milivoj Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Tomislav Jonjic, appearing for Valentin Coric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jonjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SKOBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I am Marinko Skobic, attorney-at-law from Mostar, appearing for Berislav Pusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Skobic. Then I'd like to hear from each of the accused whether he can hear me in a language that he understands. And perhaps in order to have no confusion at all, please repeat your name as well. Let's start at the first row. I think Mr. Praljak, if we start with Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm Slobodan Praljak. I can follow everything that is going on and I understand the language. Thank you. THE ACCUSED PUSIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am Berislav Pusic. I can follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pusic. Next row. THE ACCUSED PRLIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm Jadranko Prlic and I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Prlic. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm Valentin Coric. I can understand you very well and I can follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Coric. THE ACCUSED STOJIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am Bruno Stojic. I can understand and follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojic. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm Milivoj Petkovic. I am able to follow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petkovic. We are here this afternoon to have a Status Conference, to start with. During this Status Conference, we'll only deal with matters of disclosure of material from the Prosecution to the Defence, with the protection of witnesses, with your detention situation, gentlemen, and your health. If there would be any issue, especially, for example, concerning your health, you'd like to discuss rather in private session than in a public session, then please indicate so, so that I can order private session. After this Status Conference, we will have a hearing on -- also a public hearing, on the motions that have been filed on your behalf on provisional release. For this hearing, the governments of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina and of the Netherlands have been invited to attend. After that hearing, we'll have another hearing, which is not a public hearing and which does not affect all of you, only those involved will be present during this hearing. So the first thing to do now is the Status Conference. Before dealing with that, I'd first like to address all counsel. May I remind you that Rule 126 bis requires you to ask leave to respond to a response on a motion. So if there's a motion, the other party has the right to respond to that, unless otherwise ordered. But the party who filed the motion can only respond to that response with leave of the Chamber. Now and then, it seems to be the practice that, while asking leave to respond already to include in that motion all the matters the party concerned would like to raise. This Chamber would like you first to ask leave to respond to the motion. It may well be that an oral decision will be given on that, so it's not necessary that you have to wait for a couple of days before you know whether you can file such a response. Very often, this decision is conveyed to you through the intermediary of the senior legal council. But the Chamber would like to stick strictly to these rules. Then we come to the next point, disclosure. On the 17th of June, this Chamber has decided that disclosure of supporting material is deferred pending resolution of outstanding issues and we have heard the -- or read the responses by the Defence. In the decision, the Chamber has granted the Prosecution's motion and has authorised the Prosecution to defer the disclosure of the supporting material until the issues of potential conflict of interest are disposed of, and that will be soon from now on. Are there any further submissions to be made in respect of disclosure? Not for the Prosecution. Any of the Defence counsel? Since no one responds or stands, I take it that no Defence counsel has to make any submissions in this respect. Then we come to the next issue, protective measures. There is a motion pending. A decision could be soon expected. Is there any submission to be made in respect of protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Not for the Prosecution, Your Honour. I think our papers were filed and we have nothing to add to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nothing to add for the Defence, or is there anyone who would like to make any submission? If not, we'll move to our next subject, that is, the other pending motions. There are quite a lot. If I count well, there are some 14 motions pending. But mainly motions in respect of the matters we'll deal with this afternoon. You'll understand that we'll first hear the parties on those motions to see whether there's anything to be added to what has already been put on paper and then decisions will follow soon. There is one confidential motion filed by the Prosecution which might cause some delay in taking a decision on six motions filed by Defence counsel. It's not a matter to be discussed at this moment in open court. If any counsel would like to say something about that, we could do that later on in the specific hearing on those motions. That will be the second part of this afternoon's hearing, where the Chamber, although unfortunately not complete, but two out of three Judges will hear. Next issue, if there's nothing to raise in respect of what we just dealt with, is the health of the accused. I'd like to hear perhaps directly from the accused, but whatever counsel would like to add is of course welcome, and if counsel would prefer to submit whatever you'd like to submit in respect of the health of the accused, of course you're free to do so. But it's a matter that is suitable for direct communication with the accused. If any of you would like to ask for private session, that is, the public not to be aware of the matters to be discussed, please ask me. I'll first ask you, Mr. Praljak, whether you would like to raise anything in respect of your health at this moment. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I am in good health, in view of my age, apart from minor difficulties and discomforts, of course, Your Honour. But I am generally in good health.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Praljak. Mr. Pusic. I hardly have to ask you, because I'm seeing that you're using crutches. But please say what you'd like to say. THE ACCUSED PUSIC: [Interpretation] Considering that I have come from the hospital, at the summons of the Tribunal, having received inadequate assistance at the Detention Unit, inadequate to my illness, they can do no more. So I am left to my own devices, and I'm not feeling either good or bad; something in between, rather. But I have no complaints against the personnel of the Detention Unit. I would like to express my appreciation, especially for the warden of the Detention Unit, because he has shown understanding for my situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would there be any specific thing? You see, I do not get the after care that I would need. Is there any specific issue to say, well, for example, that you say, I need physiotherapy, or medication should be reviewed, or is there any specific issue you'd like to bring to my attention? THE ACCUSED PUSIC: [Interpretation] The Detention Unit cannot provide me with either physiotherapy or any further treatment. With the facilities that are available to them, they have given me the maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pusic. I'll ask specific attention, since you raised the issue of physiotherapy. I'm not aware -- I'm not a medical doctor. I do not know what is needed and what is available and to what extent something is available, but I'll certainly ask specific attention for what you just told me. Then Mr. Prlic. THE ACCUSED PRLIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no health problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Prlic. Mr. Coric. THE ACCUSED CORIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm feeling fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojic. THE ACCUSED STOJIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no health complaints. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petkovic. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the time being, I have no problems, and if any minor problems occur, my cooperation with the personnel of the Detention Unit is very good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for these answers. Then we'll move to our next subject, and that is whether there are any problems in relation to the detention circumstances. There has been a 65 ter meeting this morning with counsel, and the Senior Legal Officer has not heard any complaints. Nevertheless, I'd like to directly address you and ask whether you agree with that or whether there would be something you would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please put your microphone on. Otherwise I do not receive any translation of your words. Yes, Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Detention Unit is a highly civilised institution, and in view of that, I have absolutely no complaints against the operation of the entire organisation. Thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pusic. THE ACCUSED PUSIC: [Interpretation] As I have already said, I have no complaints against the Detention Unit in Scheveningen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In view of what has been said this morning, may I ask the others, that is, Mr. Prlic, Mr. Coric, Mr. Stojic, Mr. Petkovic, to stand if they would like to add something, and if not, I just establish at this moment that there are no complaints about your detention situation. I see that you all agree with that. This, then, concludes the Status Conference. We'll have a short break and then we'll continue the session by hearing any additional submissions in relation to the six motions requesting your provisional release.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
